# GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol Come to GitHub Copilot: What They Do

> **In short:** OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol are now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says both are built for agentic coding and code review, and that early tests showed them catching more real problems in code than earlier GPT-6 models while using fewer tokens.

If you write code, or work with people who do, you may have noticed AI tools creeping into every step of the process. Writing a function is only part of the job. Someone still has to check the work, and that is where these new models are aimed.

## What the two models are

GitHub's announcement describes two models from OpenAI, both designed for coding work.

- **GPT-6.2 Astra** is aimed at agentic coding and terminal work. "Agentic" means the AI can carry out a multi-step task on its own, such as reading files, making changes, and checking the results. "Terminal work" refers to the text-based command line where developers run programs.
- **GPT-6.2 Sol** is aimed at complex agentic coding and in-depth code review. Code review is the process of reading someone else's code to catch bugs, risky patterns, and mistakes before they reach users.

OpenAI says both models show stronger coding judgment than earlier GPT-6 models. In plain terms, they are meant to make better decisions about the code in front of them.

## What the early results say

These numbers come from the companies themselves, so treat them as their claims, not independent verdicts.

- According to the announcement, both models caught significantly more real issues in code review than earlier GPT-6 models.
- Both used fewer **tokens** to get there. A token is a small chunk of text that an AI reads and writes, and token counts often affect how much computing a task costs.
- GitHub says Sol caught nearly twice as many real issues as GPT-6.1 Sol, while keeping its findings accurate.

## Who can use them and where

According to GitHub, the models are available to users of Copilot Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise. You choose them in the **model picker**, the menu where you select which AI model a tool uses. GitHub lists many places where it appears, including Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio, the Copilot command-line tool, the Copilot coding agent, the GitHub Copilot app, github.com, GitHub Mobile on iOS and Android, JetBrains IDEs, Xcode, and Eclipse.

The rollout is gradual. If you do not see the models yet, GitHub says to check back soon.

Pricing follows usage-based billing at provider list prices. For the current rates, check the official "Models and pricing for GitHub Copilot" page instead of relying on any article, including this one.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life**: If you write code for a hobby or a side project, these models are most useful for longer tasks, such as fixing a bug across several files, where an AI that checks its own work can save you time.
- **For your business or work**: Team leads and admins can decide who gets access. GitHub says Business and Enterprise administrators can manage GPT-6.2 access through the model policy in Copilot settings. New models are switched on automatically unless an admin has turned off the global default or disabled them explicitly, so check that setting before your team starts using them.
- **If you're just getting started**: You do not need to change how you write code. Look for the model picker in your editor, pick one of the new models for a review task, and compare its notes with your own.
- **If you already use it**: Try Sol on a pull request you have already reviewed yourself. Compare what it flags with your own findings, and note the issues it caught that you missed.

## Wrap-up

GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are now available in GitHub Copilot for eligible plans, with Astra aimed at agentic coding and terminal work and Sol aimed at deeper code review. The companies report stronger results, but your own tests matter most. Your next step: open the model picker in the tool you use most, or ask your admin whether the models are enabled for your account, and try one small review task this week.
